name: Behind-the-Back Barbell Shrug
description: The behind-the-back barbell shrug places the bar behind the body against the glutes, shifting the line of force to target the mid and upper trapezius with the shoulders in a slightly retracted position. This altered angle can reduce the anterior shoulder dominance common with front-loaded shrug variations and improve the peak contraction quality of the upper traps. It is typically performed from a power rack or Smith machine for safety.

execution.starting_position: Stand with the barbell behind the body, gripped with a pronated (overhand) grip at approximately hip width. The bar rests against the upper glutes. Stand upright.
execution.setup_instructions: Best performed from a power rack with the bar set at hip height, or using a Smith machine. The range of motion is slightly more limited than a front shrug.
steps: Step 1: Unrack the bar behind the body. Stand tall with arms straight.
Step 2: Elevate the shoulders as high as possible, drawing them directly upward.
Step 3: Hold the peak contraction for one second.
Step 4: Lower the shoulders under full control to the starting position.
Step 5: Allow the shoulders to depress fully before the next rep.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the shrug upward, inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Rolling the shoulders forward or backward — the motion is straight up and straight down
Using excessive load, which prevents full elevation
Failing to lower completely between reps, limiting the total range of motion
safety_considerations: The bar can scrape the lower back if gripped too wide — use a hip-width grip
Avoid this exercise if there is any lower back or glute pain from the bar contact
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full shoulder elevation at the top, full depression at the bottom.
coaching_cues: Shrug straight up — not forward or backward
Touch your ears with your shoulders
